# All Aboard!

*Pages PDF 8-24*

## **Diplomacy on Board**
Much of this adventure involves interacting with NPCs, particularly the crew of the _Liebenswerte Adda_ . If the Characters do that well, and make friends, it will help them at the end. To keep track, use the table below. For each NPC the Characters interact with positively, track successful encounters, as this improves their relationship with that NPC. Two successful interactions will improve their relationship status by one level. Some crew, those who don’t like the cut of the Characters’ jib, need more work to start having favourable opinions about them. 

Attitudes range from Hostile, conferring a –20 penalty when using Fellowship-based Tests to engage with the NPC, to Unfriendly (–10), Cool (+0), Friendly (+10), and Best Mates (+20). 

Successful interactions may include the successful use of any Skill based on Fellowship, or any roleplaying that the GM thinks would impress the NPC in question and reassure them that the Character is acting in a friendly, trustworthy manner.

## **All Aboard!**
The scenario as written assumes the Characters have agreed to help Captain Sigiswald, and are on the docks on Odner. Read the following to the players. 

_For the folk who live on the storm-ravaged coasts of the Sea of Claws, it is a hard life, but the recent storms have been particularly harsh. Here you are on Odner, a small island off the coast of Nordland. The islanders here are busy rebuilding their homes and grieving their dead. In years past, the islanders would have taken the bodies to the nearby island of Grabufer, where a Morrite monastery and garden tended to funeral rites and interments._ 

_But Grabufer was deluged by massive waves and the mortuary was washed away along with its priests. Not only have the folk of Odner nowhere to bless and bury their dead, but several more bodies have since washed up on their muddy shores. There are twenty-three coffins arranged on the dockside, awaiting transport._ 

_The sole survivor of Grabufer’s monastic community is a portly middle-aged man with a ruddy face who wears the plain black robes of an initiate of Morr. He looks pained, but as he sees you, he plasters an ingratiating grin on his face. ‘Look lively, sailors! We need to get these stowed away and… erm… ship shape… ahaah… else they will likely grow restless before our work is done.’ He chuckles, but then he begins to blush, and wipes at his jowls with a greasy crimson handkerchief._ 

Because he is only an initiate, Brother Ammenhai does not have the _Invoke Talent_ , essential for casting the _Last Rites_ Miracle ( **WFRP** , page 223), which ensures a corpse cannot be targeted by Necromancy. This is why the journey needs to be made to Dietershafen where a capable priest can cast Last Rites. 

## **Loading the Cargo**
The Characters are expected to pitch in with shifting the coffins. There are twenty-two poor quality coffins, which have obviously been constructed in a hurry. They are nailed shut and inscribed with Morr’s religious markings. They smell heavily of incense. Each is a heavy load, requiring an Extended **Difficult (–10) Strength** Test to stow them on board the vessel, needing 4 SLs overall. Any Fumble means the carrying Character suffers a Fatigued Condition. Pierre, Snorri, Esme, Marie, Uri, and Svetlana will help with the loading, and will be impressed by Characters who perform the task of lugging coffins admirably. 

Characters who announce that they are keeping a close eye on their shipmates may notice on a **Hard (–20) Perception** Test that a brief scuffle breaks out between Esme and Svetlana. The Halfling starts to lug at a coffin when the Ostlander pulls it from her grasp and snarls: ‘ _Don’t strain yourself, Halfling, leave the heavy lifting to those who can manage it.’_ 

If anyone attempts to intercede, Svetlana just complains that she is concerned for the Halfling’s welfare, and doesn’t think that she should be doing too much heavy lifting. In reality, Svetlana just wants to keep a close eye on where this particular coffin, which contains stolen goods, ends up. Once the load is stowed away, Svetlana does not show any concern over how hard Esme or Marie work. Anyone examining this coffin will notice on a **Hard (–20) Perception** Test that there is a small ‘x’ carved in the lower right corner of each panel of the coffin. 

Should anyone attempt to break into this coffin, Brother Ammenhai will do all he can to dissuade them, claiming that the coffins and body wrappings have been designed so as to prevent the dead from rising, and that any disturbance will risk nullifying their effects. If Characters persist they find that the coffin contains brass fittings and silverware worth about 15 GC. 

_From above, the captain takes a moment to watch your labours, puffing on a big pipe. He looks up, squints at the sky, and moves out of sight._ 

Any Character interested in the captain’s behaviour may make a **Hard (–20) Perception** Test. Those who pass spot a large seabird flying north. The captain is a superstitious fellow and considers the fact that an albatross has flown past the vessel at this time to be inauspicious. 

_The final coffin is a more elaborate affair — it is carved with black roses and embossed images of hourglasses and skulls. Next to it is a large chest smelling strongly of incense._ 

If the Characters query what’s in the last coffin Brother Ammenhai chuckles nervously and then adopts a pose of mock seriousness. He says, ‘ _None of your beeswax — just get it on board. Don’t worry, you’ll get what’s coming to you. The garden of Morr in Dietershafen will be sure to provide you with reimbursement for your efforts.’_ 

It’s a **Difficult (–10) Strength** Test to bring this final cargo on board. If a Character tries to peek into the coffin, they find the lid is firmly nailed down, just like the others. It looks more ornate, as if more care had been taken in choosing it, perhaps out of respect for the contents. This coffin contains the corpse of Brother Ammenhai’s wife. There is no sinister reason for his attitude towards the coffin, though he has shown her preferential treatment. If Characters show suspicion about the coffin, he will be _‘the body_ defensive at first and then admit that it contains _of my beloved Erika_ ’. If Characters insist on searching the coffin, he resents them for it, and protests, but he doesn’t have the authority to actually prevent them. It contains exactly what he says it contains. 

Once the job is done, there is a little free time to spend before the ship sets sail. The crew take time to pay their respects at a nearby small shrine to Manann, God of the Sea. If the Characters join them, they will regard it as proper behaviour. There is also some time to spend gossiping with the locals working the docks. 

## **Dockside Scuttlebutt**
If the Characters wish to spend a bit of time chatting to the locals, there is the opportunity to do so. The folk of Odner are normally gregarious and friendly, if rather contemptuous of those who are not wise in the ways of the sea. 

However, they have recently undergone much hardship and are busy repairing their shattered dwellings and boats. There are a couple of subjects the locals will be happy to talk about, and they even volunteer these opinions in passing as the Characters work loading the coffins. 

- Brother Ammenhai is only an initiate, and lacks the ability to ensure a corpse cannot be targeted by Necromancy. It will soon be Geheimnisnacht, when the Chaos Moon is full and the dead do not rest easy, so please work away and Manann speed you on your journey. 

- The recent storms were terrible. When you're underway be sure to keep an eye out for flotsam. We’ve a ship unaccounted for, the _Einzelgänger_ . It’s been gone several days and we fear it is wrecked. 

Getting more than a brisk response from them requires a **Difficult (–10) Gossip** Test. 

- Only a fool would set sail on Geheimnisnacht; evil sails the seas and thirsts for blood. 

- Some of the bodies washed up had been chewed up by something. Probably the Grey-Barbed Shark of the Sea of Claws. It has a taste for the flesh of seafolk. 

_As the sun sinks into the sea, the captain blows a shrill whistle. ‘All aboard who’s coming aboard!’ He looks at you with watery brown eyes above a strawberry nose._ 

Once aboard, any Characters who announce that they are keeping an eye on things may make a **Difficult (–10) Perception** Test to observe the following: 

_A woman wearing a hooded cloak sidles up to the gangplank. She exchanges a few short words with Svetlana, who is busying herself by taking care of the mooring ropes that secure the ship to the harbour. Svetlana nods, and hands the woman a small leather pouch._ 

A character passing a **Difficult (–10) Perception** Test hears the clink of coins in the pouch. If Svetlana is confronted about this interaction she will claim the woman was Odner’s harbourmaster, and the money was to pay for the berth of the ship. Uri will back Svetlana up, but if other members of the crew are consulted they will be confused — after all, the crew of the vessel are doing the residents of Odner a significant favour by helping them out, and the harbourmaster is a man. 

This may develop into an argument with Svetlana, who is not widely liked amongst the crew, but Captain Sigiswald breaks up any fights before they turn violent, promising that any wrongdoing can be investigated in Dietershafen. 

In reality the woman on the docks is a local smuggler, and Svetlana has paid her for the work she has done bringing her the coffin full of stolen items. 

- Years ago ‘round this time, we’d be taking in the Daggerfish catch ‘round now, but it’s been harder and harder to catch them, and now with this storm, there’s no hope. 

- If you ever get to Salzenmund, I hope you can give those fools at the Grand Orrery a piece of my mind. Each month they are supposed to send us a forecast warning of inclement weather, but the last missive just said the winds would be ‘moderate or rough’ and that ‘Azyr in particular may be unpredictable’. What use is that? 

## **The Liebenswerte Adda**

- The galley is Rutger’s domain. He spends most of his time here preparing food and taking stock. He does not appreciate company, so tells folk to leave him to his work unless a meal is being served. 

Once the Characters are on board there is the chance to look around and get to know the ship and her crew. Whilst the captain wishes to depart as soon as possible, he is delayed in this until the winds turn, and it is late in the afternoon, about 5 o’clock, before the vessel finally makes its way from Odner’s harbour. 

- Pierre does not like letting Characters into the armoury. Anyone searching it will notice that there are only 15 cannonballs in the armoury, and that many of the barrels of blackpowder have suffered from damp conditions and have become useless.

- The officers do not like to be bothered unless there is an emergency that demands attention. Their attitudes vary from good-humoured but firm dismissal (Captain Sigiswald), to maudlin dismissal (Bosun Snorri), to making angry remarks about being harangued by landlubbers (First Mate Fiorella). 

The _Liebenswerte Adda_ is a small cog and, whilst it is kept ship-shape, it shows signs of wear and tear. Characters who show an interest in the ship may find out the following simply by looking around. Much of the adventure takes place on the open main deck, which has an upper deck with a forecastle at the prow (front), and a quarterdeck at the stern (back). Belowdecks, there is the lower deck with cabins and the galley, and below that the slimy hold which contains the ship’s ballast and its ravenous rodent population that keep Mieze entertained. 

   - The rest of the crew also prioritise their duties over gossiping with the Characters, though they will appreciate any assistance they are given. 

   - Brother Ammenhai insists that someone be present in the hold with the coffins at all times. He is willing to attend during the First Dog Watch and Second Dog Watch. 

- Upon the quarterdeck, there is a mounted brass telescope. This is also where the wheel to steer the ship is located.

- The ship is armed with 4 medium cannon, two to each side, with which to ward off pirates and sea monsters. Ammunition is stored belowdecks in the magazine, but it has not been replenished for a long time and much of the blackpowder is ruined. 

- Sleeping quarters are rather luxurious for a ship of this size. The captain has his own cabin, another is shared between Svetlana and Uri, and other cabins containing room to hang four hammocks are shared out between the rest of the crew and the Characters. Pierre prefers to keep to himself, and tends to sleep in the ship’s armoury. The cabins, armoury, galley, and brig are all on the second deck of the vessel, beneath the main deck and above the hold. 

- The hold is lined with a layer of deep shingle to help stabilise the boat and cushion the crates of food and barrels of water and beer that are stored here. The coffins are placed here, to the rear of the ship. The smell of the bodies, mixed with the pong of the various substances that have leached down into the hold over the years, is… piquant… to say the least. 

## **First Dog Watch**
As the _Liebenswerte Adda_ sets sail amid high winds and rough seas, Characters who are not used to sailing must Test for Sea Sickness. 

## **Sea Sickness**
Most folk get seasick when they first sail, but anyone who sticks at it soon gets used to the rocking of the waves. Elves seem to be immune to its effect, as is any Character with the _Sea Legs_ Talent. 

**Contraction:** Whenever any Human, Dwarf, Halfling, or Ogre Character first undertakes a journey at sea, they must make a **Difficult (–10) Endurance** Test or suffer from sea sickness. In rough weather (Strong Gales or Violent Storms), such Characters should make a **Challenging (+0) Endurance** Test or suffer from sea sickness as well. 

**Duration:** For sea sickness due to being new to seafaring, make a **Challenging (+0) Endurance** Test after each day at sea. If the Test is passed, the Character will not suffer this form of sea sickness again. For sea sickness resulting from rough seas or other temporary effects, make a **Challenging (+0) Endurance** Test every hour. 

## **Symptoms:** Malaise, Nausea.
Brother Ammenhai wishes to have the Characters accompany him into the hold so that he can show them how to prepare the censers with incense and chant a liturgy to Morr. 

Esme, being a rather generous sort of Halfling, volunteers to take the Middle Watch. Uri and Svetlana also volunteer to help, but they are more interested in ensuring that they recover their smuggled goods than they are with chanting soothing songs to the dead. 

_The priest ambles over, dabbing at his sweaty face with a red handkerchief. ‘Now remember, you’re being well paid to tend my precious cargo. Refresh them regularly with incense and sing songs of mourning.’ Then he demonstrates how to fill the censers with incense and to intone a few of the more common prayers to Morr._ 

## **Second Dog Watch**
Normally a trip from Odner to Dietershafen could be completed in under ten hours, but a strong offshore wind is blowing and the boat is making very slow progress. 

Any Character who passes a **Challenging (+0) Navigation** Test is able to tell that the vessel is making little headway, and is mostly fighting against the wind just to maintain its position. 

The crew are cautious about taking efforts to speed their journey. They say it is a short distance to Dietershafen, but that the seas are treacherous and it would be unwise to proceed without caution. 

After a couple of hours Captain Sigiswald calls for the anchor to be dropped. Read the following to the Characters. 

_You hear the ship’s bell being rung with urgency, and looking toward the poop deck you see the captain calling for attention. ‘There be little sense in trying to make more headway tonight, not under these conditions. Trim the sails, drop the anchor, batten the hatches, and join me belowdecks.’_ 

The crew soon assemble in the galley. When the Characters enter, read the following: 

_The galley is cramped and shadowy, gloomily lit by flickering lanterns. The rickety table is covered in a stained white cloth and is laid out with chipped crockery and glassware, though the cutlery, to your surprise, seems to be a fine set of silver knives, forks, and spoons. Rutger the cook serves up bowls of stew, made from beets and preserved meat. The meat is tough and salty, and though it is filling, its provenance is rather obvious, as the occasional bristly pig’s ear, or knuckle, can be discerned in the stew._ 

The repast is fortifying, and those who join in can remove any _Fatigued_ Conditions they are suffering from. Brother Ammenhai does not attend dinner; he is down in the hold with the coffins. 

## **Table Talk**
During the meal there is little small talk other than that which the Characters introduce themselves. There are a few interactions though. 

_Friedrich the ship’s boy seems full of mischief. He glares about the table and says: ‘Seeing as the Night of Mystery is nearly upon us, does anyone know any stories of restless spirits?’_ 

_The captain is angry._ 

_‘Don’t make light of the unquiet dead, boy! Something I’ll never forget until my dying day, I was taking a moonlit watch when I felt a chilly dread come over me. I thought I heard something, but knew it was just me and the sickly light of Morrslieb for company. Over the railing I saw a dripping sailor climb, in tattered clothes, and of ghostly aspect. I was frozen in terror. It took the wheel beside me, as if it were its turn to guide the ship safely through the long dark night. It stayed there until morning, then slipped back over the rail into the mist, without a sound, leaving naught but bony wet footprints on the deck.’_ 

## **First Watch**
How the rest of the night passes depends a lot on the activities of the Characters. Brother Ammenhai expects them to help him keep watch over the coffins and replenish the censers of incense he has set up near them. However, only one Character is needed to do this at any particular time. 

Friedrich loves of practical jokes. If Characters are asleep in their cabin, he tries to give them a scare by leaving a trail of skeletal footprints leading from their room to the hold. He hopes to convince them that something has risen from one of the coffins and is wandering around. Once he has made the prints, he stands outside their door and makes what he thinks are ‘zombie groans’. It is a **Hard (–20) Perception** Test to hear him, though he will try three times. If the door is flung open the Character should make **Challenging (+0) Perception** Test. 1 SL is enough to spot the prints on the floor, but 4 or more SL will also mean that the Character spots Friedrich hiding further up the corridor, trying to suppress his giggles. 

## **In the Hold — Part 1**
The Character who has volunteered to watch over the coffins in the hold should be told the following as they get close to the area. 

_The cabin boy is staring, eyes wide like saucers, chin dropped._ 

_‘Of course, no one believed me — they thought I’d been at the rum again. But I asked about it and I heard that when a ship crosses the place a sailor was lost at sea, they like to climb back aboard and continue what they were doing before. It puts them at peace. So, I do believe in spirits — well, since then anyway.’_ 

_The smell down here is now an overwhelming mixture of cloying scents: stagnant brine, spilled ale, dead flesh, and pungent incense._ 

The Character should then Test to see if they succumb to seasickness, even if they passed such a Test before. Provided that they pass, they can be told the following: 

_You can hear Brother Ammenhai within the hold, softly singing a chanty._ 

If the Character wishes to stop and listen more closely to the priest they may make a **Stealth** Test Opposed by Ammenhai’s **Perception** . If they fail, the priest realises they are there and stops singing. If not, they hear the following words: 

_‘She sells seashells on the seashore, until sharky caught her selling, and now she sells no more, as she’s lying silently, on the shelly seafloor.’_ 

This is certainly not one of the prayers to Morr the priest taught the Characters earlier. If the Characters take issue with this, the captain decides it is a matter for the port authorities, so everyone should stay calm and carry on. He offers everyone a tot of rum and takes two tots himself. 

## **In the Hold — Part 2**
As it grows closer to midnight, the shadows belowdecks seem to become bigger and darker. A Character passing an **Average (+20) Perception** Test sees something moving furtively in the darkest corner, and a swish of a rat-like tail. Ask any Characters on watch, in Initiative order, what they want to do. Suddenly Mieze leaps out of the darkness and deposits a dead rodent at the feet of a Character. The cat then saunters off, tail up, back on patrol. 

## **Middle Watch**
If any Characters are on deck during this time, they may make a **Challenging (+0) Perception** Test in order to spot something in the water. A man clinging to a large piece of flotsam. If no Characters are on deck, or pass the test, Svetlana calls out as follows: 

_Svetlana cries out ‘Man over-board’ and points to the starboard bow where a man can be seen clinging to some driftwood. He’s not moving. The captain puffs on his pipe, considering the situation. ‘Looks dead to me. Let’s press on.’ A raven lazily flaps over and starts pecking at the body, but the man feebly brushes it away._ 

If no one argues to rescue the man, the ship sails on, leaving the poor soul to his fate. If the Characters press a case to rescue him, the captain reluctantly agrees for the first mate to take the rowboat out with the Characters to perform a rescue mission. 

_Out on the endless ocean, you feel small and insignificant. Sounds travel strangely across the water. The ravens caw listlessly, and you hear snippets of conversation from the ship._ 

The sea is choppy, and two Characters need to pass a **Difficult (–10) Row** Test to reach the man. A Fumble means they fall overboard, feel something big brush their leg, and need to pass a **Challenging (+0) Athletics** Test to haul themselves back on the boat. Fiorella curses their useless landlubber ways. When they reach the man, read the following: 

_You can tell this man has been through a lot. His muscular body is covered in scars and matted body hair, his clothing tattered, and his face crusted with salt. One big green eye opens slowly at your approach, and he begs to be given a drink of water._ 

The Characters can extract his name, Fenris, and his ship’s name, the _Einzelgänger_ . He is close to unconsciousness, and after providing a few answers his gaze turns to Morrslieb, which appears gibbous and low from behind a cloud. ‘ _Beware the moon!_ ’ he mutters, and falls into a stupor. 

Back on the boat, the captain suggests that Fenris be confined to the brig. If Characters check in on Fenris later, he’s snarling in his dreams, revealing long yellow teeth. 

## **The Shadow of the Shadewraith**
Whilst the encounter with Captain Fenris distracts the crew, any Character who announces that they are remaining on deck during the Middle Watch may be able to glimpse a sight of the _Shadewraith_ as it patrols the Sea of Claws. 

During the night, a thick fog descends on the ship, and it is difficult to see far through the enveloping mist. However, any Character who does keep watch can be called on to make a **Difficult (–10) Perception** Test. If they use the telescope on the foredeck, the Test is **Average (+20)** instead. If they pass, read them the following: 

_Far out into the distance, something catches your eye: a lambent greenish glow can be seen playing on the far horizon. As you continue to watch, a shape begins to form. It looks like the rotten remains of a vast galleon. Holed and rotten sails drape from its mast, and its hull is reduced to splintered beams and bulkheads, yet still it sails, not so much upon the waves themselves, but floating some yards above them. It is lit by a strange green inner light._ 

Once spotted, the _Shadewraith_ spends six turns bearing towards the Character, but then veers to port and sails for another six turns in parallel to the _Liebenswerte Adda_ , before vanishing in the fog. If any of the NPC crew are roused in time to see the _Shadewraith,_ they will be disturbed at the sight, but if they are roused after it has passed, they will not find the story of the sighting convincing. 

## **Captain Fenris**
Fenris is a captain and part-time smuggler who used to pilot his ship, the _Einzelgänger_ , between the ports of the Nordland and the Bjornling coast of Norsca. He is solidly built, and conspicuously hairy. 

Fenris has a Dooming that he interprets as meaning he will be drowned one Geheimnisnacht, and as a result, he is rather obsessed with the moon, and desperate to reach dry land before the night falls. This desperation has caused him to make a rash journey in harsh weather. Unfortunately this has had tragic consequences. His ship has been wrecked and his crew lost.

## **The Murder**
At some point during the Middle Watch, Brother Ammenhai murders Pierre. Ammenhai is eager to repay his debt to Stromfels, and Pierre is isolated due to his preference for sleeping alone, as well as being physically weak. 

However, Pierre is a vigilant and fierce man, for all his lack of size, and even when taken by surprise by the brother in the middle of the night, he is able to jab the priest with his penknife before succumbing to strangulation. 

- Shortly before the murder, Ammenhai unlocks the door to the brig. He hopes to blame the murder on Captain Fenris. If any Character is keeping watch over this area, Brother Ammenhai does not unlock the brig, and attempts to sneak off without being noticed. 

- The murder takes place at 3 AM. Brother Ammenhai strangles Pierre in his bunk in the ship’s armoury, taking a deep cut to his left forearm in the process. 

- At 3:15 AM, Ammenhai drags Pierre’s body up from the armoury and secretes it in a cubby hole near the main exit onto the main deck. He leaves spatters of his own blood behind him as he does so. 

- He then wraps his arm up in his red handkerchief to staunch the bleeding, and walks about on the main deck. If any of the Characters are on the main deck he tells them he heard a disturbance from the brig. 

- If he can get time alone on deck, Ammenhai will drag Pierre’s body to the side of the boat, and throw him overboard. 

- At 3:30 AM Ammenhai will then return to the brig and wipe blood over the doorway. If he was unable to unlock the door earlier, he will now. If anyone is in the brig with Fenris, he will instead sneak off as earlier. 

At the end of the escapade, Ammenhai has left the following clues: 

- Spatters of blood line the corridor leading from the armoury to the deck of the vessel. These may be spotted by anyone who uses the corridor and passes an **Average (+20) Perception** Test. 

- Brother Ammenhai previously used to constantly wipe at his face with a red handkerchief, which is now used to bandage a short but deep cut on his left forearm. 

- If he was able to get to the brig without interference, Brother Ammenhai smeared blood on the door, though there is no blood inside, and none on Captain Fenris. 

## **Morning Watch**
Svetlana has volunteered to watch over the coffins during this period. She uses this time to open the coffin marked with small Xs, retrieve the stolen goods, stash them in her cabin, and return to the hold to nail shut the coffin again. Every time Svetlana makes a journey from the hold to her cabin, she passes the Characters’ cabin. A Character who is awake will hear her on an **Average (+20) Perception** Test. A Character who is asleep will hear her on a **Very Hard (–30) Perception** Test. 

- At 4:30 AM, Svetlana pries up the lid of the coffin and unwraps the treasure from the body wrappings. 

- At 4:45 AM, Svetlana carries a brass lantern and a silver candlestick holder from the hold to her cabin. If disturbed, she says she heard some sounds on deck and is going to investigate. 

- At 5 AM, Svetlana carries a box of silver jewellry and a small brass statue of a fish from the hold to her cabin. If disturbed, she repeats her story about noises on deck. 

- At 5:15 AM, Svetlana carries a high quality telescope and cutlass from the hold to her cabin. This time if she is apprehended, she claims that she fell asleep during her watch, and woke to find one of the coffins is open. She fears that one of the dead has risen, and is searching for it. 

- At 5:20 AM, Mieze creeps into the empty coffin, makes a bed from the wrappings, and falls asleep. 

- At 5:30 AM, Svetlana returns to the coffin and taps the lid shut again, unwittingly trapping the sleeping cat within. 

## **Forenoon Watch**
As dawn breaks, the waves have turned rough. Each Character aside from Elves and those with the Sea Legs Talent must Test to see if they suffer from Sea Sickness again. However, the winds have altered direction, and whilst the fog remains thick around the vessel, the captain orders that the ship be readied to set sail once more. 

## **In the Hold — Part 3**
The Character who is undertaking the watch in the hold has not been at their post for long before they hear frenzied scratching sounds emanating from the coffin marked with small Xs. If the lid of the coffin is prized up, read the following to the Character: 

_There are some scuffling sounds. Looking closer you see two evil green eyes in the dark, staring right back at you, unblinking._ 

Ask your Players what they want to do, in Initiative order. 

_Suddenly the lid shifts, then clatters to the floor, as Mieze springs out and immediately scampers off._ 

There is nothing in the coffin other than some loose body wrappings. What the Characters make of this occurrence is up to them, but if the crew are told of this, they will assume the Characters are playing some sort of trick on them, and will become less friendly towards them. 

## **The Rudder Incident**
_The fog is thickening into what the folk of Albion call a real pea souper. The captain can be heard loudly cussing. Up on the quarterdeck, he explains that the rudder has become stuck, and he can no longer steer the ship. Someone needs to go in the water to fix it, else they’ll be going nowhere fast._ 

None of the crew volunteer. The Characters should realise it is time for a swimmer amongst them to be brave. 

_You are tied to a long rope. The captain clasps you firmly on the shoulder and says, ‘Don’t dilly dally down there. Just free the rudder, then tug three times and we’ll pull you up.’_ 

If the Characters look to Brother Ammenhai for divine support, he attempts to cast the Blessing of Breath or Blessing of Fortune ( **WFRP** , page 221). Note the risk of incurring the Wrath of the Gods. 

The Character must pass an **Easy (+40) Swim** Test to reach the jammed rudder a few fathoms underwater. A **Challenging (+0) Perception** Test is needed to locate the problem’s cause, which is a small body jammed in the rudder. A **Difficult (–10) Cool** Test is needed to avoid gasping and starting to drown ( **WFRP** , page 181). It’s then a **Hard (–20) Strength** Test to work the body free, which can be made much easier, an **Average (+20) Strength** Test, using the knife (still in the corpse’s grasp), but that causes much blood to go into the water. 

Job done, and it’s three tugs to get pulled up on the rope, presumably taking the body with them to investigate its identity — unless the knife was used, in which case a shark attacks them. The shark is interested in attacking the body rather than the living diver, but if it is attacked it will bite back. It takes three rounds to get back on board. Characters on deck can try and distract the shark with ranged weapons. 

## **Grey-Barbed Shark**
| M | WS | BS | S | T | I | Ag | Dex | Int | WP | Fel | W |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 55 | – | 60 | 55 | 30 | 25 | 35 | 10 | 30 | – | 38 |

**Traits:** Armour 1 (6), Belligerent, Bestial, Frenzy, Hungry, Marine Creature, Size (Large), Stealthy, Weapon (Teeth) +10 

_Back on deck, cold and dripping wet, the captain says, ‘Good show, sailor’, but everyone else just stares at the body._ 

If the body is retrieved and brought on deck it is quickly identified as Pierre’s. A Character passing a **Difficult (–10) Heal** Test can identify marks on the man’s neck consistent with strangulation. If the shark mauled the body by biting it three times or more this becomes a **Very Hard (–30) Heal** Test. 

## **Afternoon Watch**
_Geheimnisnacht approaches. The fog clears but lightning plays across the skies. Suddenly there is a ringing of the bell and a frightened cry from the crow’s nest, ‘Ship Ahoy! Ship Ahoy!’ Those who look to the water see the form of a mighty ghostly galleon bearing down on them at speed. Its sails are tattered and threadbare, and an ethereal green light plays about its decks. It floats high above the waves, borne aloft by a host of wailing souls._ 

If the Characters look for the captain, they find his cabin locked. They can hear heavy snoring. The captain is flat out drunk on the floor, snoring heavily, empty rum bottles beside him. 

_The first mate takes command. She rushes to the quarterdeck to look through the telescope. Fiorella goes pale as the sails, and says, ‘It’s a cursed ship of the dead. Our captain has crawled inside a bottle. What should we do? Flee, or fight, or something else?’_ 

The Characters can try to sway the NPCs’ opinion about the best chance for surviving. Anyone friendly votes for their plan, anyone hostile against. Anyone neutral needs persuading. Fiorella, as acting captain, has the deciding vote. But they’d better be quick, as the _Shadewraith_ is bearing down on them. Ask the Characters what they want to do. 

- **Prepare for battle.** Did they find cannonballs? Fiorella orders Snorri to take the weapons from the captain’s locker, giving spares to the Characters. Any warrior Character will doubt they can make a dent in the _Shadewraith_ or its crew. 

- **Flee!** There may be a chance to outrun the oncoming vessel. 

- **Abandon ship.** Svetlana and Uri are working the pulleys and ropes to swing the ship’s rowboat into the water. 

- **Negotiate.** Maybe if they talk nicely to this ghost ship’s captain, he’ll let them go? 

Something else. If the Characters have a cunning plan, this is the moment for that. 

## **Black Sails Ahead**
If the Characters wish to confront the _Shadewraith,_ it is a frightening prospect, though they may be able to see it off with spells or cannonfire. Note that in order to arm the ship’s cannons, the Characters will have to locate good gunpowder. This means going to the armoury and passing a **Difficult (–10) Trade (Alchemist or Engineer)** Test or **Hard (-20) Lore (Science)** Test, success meaning that a good barrel of gunpowder is located. If the Test is failed, or if no Character has such Skills, roll d100 for any barrel of gunpowder selected. On a 55 or less, the powder is spoiled and does not fire. 

In all likelihood, the _Shadewraith_ will get the better of the _Liebenswerte Adda_ , though the Characters may be able to gain some advantage due to their spells, fighting prowess, or expert seamanship. If they escape, then allowing them to make port at Dietershafen may be anticlimactic, but it would also be well earned. 

If, however, the _Shadewraith_ subdues the _Liebenswerte Adda,_ read the following: 

_There is a massive boom as the_ Shadewraith _opens fire! All the ravens fly away, a susurration of black wings. There’s a terrible crack. The main mast falls in ghastly slow motion, lit by lightning. The ship rolls alarmingly, almost turning turtle before it rights itself. As your faces tip towards the turbulent sea you see black fins, dead eyes, and big jagged teeth._ 

_An evil, sneering voice fills the air, ‘You carry a cargo of lost souls. Surrender them to me, Vangheist of the_ Shadewraith _. You cannot flee, you cannot fight, you can but die if you defy me.’_ 

## **Dealing with the Dead**
If none of the Characters work out what Vangheist means, another member of the crew, most likely Svetlana or Uri, can figure it out for them. 

_‘He’s after a cargo of souls. Do the dead still have souls? If we give those to Vangheist, we could save ours!’_ 

Fiorella is vehemently against this idea. It sounds like Necromancy. The rest of the crew can be persuaded. Any religious character will believe that until the proper rites are said, by a _capable_ priest of Morr, the soul remains in the body, just quiescent. If they ask Brother Ammenhai, he confirms this. 

If the Characters decide to negotiate, they can run up a black flag to call for parlay, and the Shadewraith stops its attack. 

The Characters row off to parlay with Vangheist. The seas are choppy, requiring two Characters to pass a **Difficult (–10) Row** Test, with Fumbles resulting in falling overboard. 

## **Parlay with the Pirate Lord**
_Your tiny boat draws up below the scabrous hull of the rotting Shadewraith, which is floating above the water, as if the sea itself is repulsed by its foul existence. A long seaweed rope, rotting and icy to the touch, is thrown down to you by a skeletal pirate._ 

To swallow down terror and climb up onto the ghastly galleon, Characters need to pass a **Hard (–20) Cool** Test. Climbing up is an **Average (+20) Climb** Test. 

_You climb over the ship’s rail and onto the rotting deck of the dread vessel, right beside an antique cannon. Decaying undead pirates surround you, shuffling, swaying, and groaning. The captain stalks forward, a corroded cutlass in each hand. ‘So you’re here to bargain with Vangheist. Well, I am feeling whimsical tonight, so I’ll hear your offer.’_ 

The Characters must negotiate with Vangheist for their souls. Have your Players roleplay this spooky encounter to the full. The best final ‘price’, or ‘unrepeatable Geheimnisnacht bargain’ as he puts it, that Vangheist will accept is all the quiescent souls from the dead bodies, plus _one_ mortal soul. If the party negotiates badly, he asks for _three_ . 

_Svetlana looks sternly at you and says, ‘Well he’s not going to have my soul! Any volunteers?’_ 

Unless a Character offers to relinquish their soul, Vangheist graciously gives them an hour to decide. They row back to the _Liebenswerte Adda_ to work out who will sacrifice themself. 

The Characters need to reach agreement with the crew about whose souls will be sacrificed. If the Characters make immoral choices, such as choosing to sacrifice an innocent, they gain a Corruption Point ( **WFRP** , page 182). If a Player decides to sacrifice their Character for the greater good, reward that noble action as if they had died in a fashion that matches their Dooming ( **WFRP** , page 136). If no Character is brave, and if he is still alive, _I’m just_ Fenris offers his soul up. His final words are, ‘ _going overboard for a little while._ ’ 

_At precisely one hour, there’s the deep chime of a ship’s bell, followed by another boom from the Shadewraith, this time taking a chunk out of the quarterdeck. Vangheist’s disembodied voice floats across the sea, ‘It’s time. Who will be joining my jolly crew on this fine Geheimnisnacht?’_ 

Once the Characters have made their decision, they return to the _Shadewraith_ with the bodies and the sacrifice. _Welcome aboard,_ Vangheist doffs his tattered hat and says, ‘ _me hearties_ ’ to his new crew. 

## **Conclusion**
Finally, the party reaches dry land at Dietershafen. If the _Liebenswerte Adda_ didn’t sink, then the crew have it repaired, and it’s soon ready to sail again. 

If a Character sacrificed themself for the greater good, the story of the party’s heroism spreads across the Sea of Claws, earning them good fortune in their next few ports of call. 

## **Awarding Experience**
In addition to points for good roleplaying and clever ideas during the session, XP should be awarded for the following: 

- 15 points for interacting well with the NPCs and making some become friendly 

- 15 points for uncovering that Brother Ammenhai is the murderer 

- 10 points to the character who unblocked the rudder 

- 10 points for revealing Svetlana to be a smuggler 

- 10 points for negotiating well with Captain Vangheist 

- 5 points for saving Fenris 

- 5 points for sailing the ship safely into port 

## **The Arch–traitor Vangheist**
From the smallest Norscan encampment to turbulent Sartosa, sailors everywhere share stories of a doomed ship. Crewed by the souls of traitors, carried by winds which no mortal can feel, _The Shadewraith_ drifts above the world’s oceans, a silent spectre which even Manann is loath to touch. 

Such a dread ship could only be captained by one with a reputation to match. The Arch-Traitor Vangheist is such _Shadewraith_ a captain. Those who have glimpsed the and lived describe a haggard figure clinging to its wheel, burning eyes fixed on the horizon. Some speculate Vangheist is searching for a means to break his curse. 

In life, Vangheist was captain of the _Stormbreaker_ and a skilled privateer. He was chartered by Albrechtus von Zeich, a mage from the Order of Light, to carry him to the world’s most northerly shores. He did not reveal his purpose, but had the entire crew, captain included, swear loyalty to him by Manann’s own spring waters. They would not question him, nor disobey his orders until they had completed his task and delivered him safely home. To make the deal palatable, each sailor was paid handsomely. With a purse of gold, and what Vangheist assumed would be a comfortable journey ferrying this rich academic, the privateer gladly swore his oath. 

Von Zeich led them deep into frigid waters, battling through ice and twisted creatures touched by Chaos. Still, he would not share what he sought. At last, Vangheist’s curiosity got the better of him. He had his first mate sneak into Von Zeich’s quarters as he entertained the mage at dinner. There, the man found a book bound in leather which, despite the cold, was warm to the touch. Its words twisted themselves on the page and, though the mate could not read, he found their meaning pouring into his mind. The mage sought a serpent made of fire. This thing, so the book said, was a guardian, protecting the way to eternal life. 

From this moment, Von Zeich’s fate was sealed. The promise of eternal life was far too great an opportunity for Vangheist to let slip away. When at last they found the great wyrm of fire, defeating it with cannon shot and arcane spells, Vangheist refused the mage’s order to turn for home. Instead, he shot the man in the back and kicked his body over the railing. Together, he and his crew sailed on, following the routes described by Von Zeich’s book. 

What they found, no one will ever know. The dead keep their secrets. They sailed for what seemed centuries, passing across seas and skies which turned themselves into twisting faces and screaming winds. Their bodies aged and withered; their ship rotted beneath them. But still they pressed on, until direction lost meaning and they sailed _Stormbreaker_ the seas of Morrslieb itself. By the time The returned to the mortal realm, nothing remained of it save its spirit. It had become the _Shadewraith_ . 

Now, Vangheist has returned to the piratical ways he followed in life. His ship preys upon lone vessels, dragging away souls to join in his torment. None have ever discerned any purpose in such attacks, the _Shadewraith_ appearing and disappearing almost at random. Captains often like to say Vangheist comes for mutineers, and that the Arch-Traitor can tell if you harbour treacherous thoughts, but the truth of this is somewhat suspect, given the sources. 

Recently, however, there have been more sightings of the _Shadewraith_ off Tilea’s coast. Vangheist’s ship, carried through the air upon the backs of the damned, has even been reported attacking towns and villages, locking stillliving people in its hold to take them who knows where. These actions go against all previously observed behaviour of the ghost ship, and are beginning to worry those who study such matters. Either the Arch-Traitor is not as aimless as previously thought, or some master of the dead has taken up his strings.
